Synopsis:
Canada's Q2 2026 GDP grew at an annualized 3.3% — the strongest pace since 2023 — driven by a 3.6% surge in exports, a rebound in household consumption (+0.8%), and the first business investment expansion in 18 months (+2.3%). Q1 was revised up to +0.3%, avoiding a technical recession. However, a new 50% U.S. tariff on $20bn of Canadian exports, imposed the same week, injects fresh uncertainty into the outlook. Markets priced in no BoC rate change. The advance estimate shows July GDP largely flat.
